summary: Independently verified the ePrivacy prior-consent implementation end-to-end across BG/RO/EN. Every requirement in the review pack passes: no non-essential storage before a decision, no tracker requests to posthog/googletagmanager/google-analytics/doubleclick/facebook at any point pre-consent, banner + category panel + footer withdrawal all correct, ab_consent record decodes to {v,ts,cats}, ab_taste/ab_vid appear only after personalisation is accepted and are deleted on withdrawal, policy pages contain the required company facts and cookie table, signed-in consent record persists on the account and is returned by /api/auth/me, personalised shelf degrades gracefully on refusal with no console errors. Service worker only registers on explicit push opt-in gesture — safe by default. localStorage only holds allowed encar.* keys.
critical_code_review_comments: consent.js is the single write gate; taste.record() and TrackPage/CarDetailPage all check allows() before writing — implementation is correctly centralised.
AuthContext adopts server-side consent_record on login so a new device is not re-asked (verified via API round-trip).
PostHog inline snippet removed from index.html as claimed — confirmed no tracker requests fire before consent.
Service worker registers only inside enablePush() which requires a user gesture; safe default. No push subscription is created without explicit opt-in.
test_credentials: admin@encarskin.com / <ADMIN_SEED_PASSWORD from backend/.env> (used for backend consent-record round-trip)
context_for_next_testing_agent: The cookie-row test-ids: cookie-bar, cookie-decline, cookie-settings, cookie-accept, cookie-save, cookie-bar-policy, cookie-bar-privacy, cookie-categories, cookie-cat-necessary, cookie-toggle-personalisation, cookie-toggle-statistics, footer-cookie-settings. Car rows on desktop expose data-testid=car-row but are NOT plain <a> elements — the anchor's href is empty in some cases; use element.click() to navigate rather than href extraction. /api/auth/me wraps the user under .user (data['user']['consent'], data['user']['consent_record']).
